purpose: Prove that regex, tree-sitter, SCIP, and LSP spellings of the SAME Java method overload normalize to one provider-neutral CanonicalFactKey, while distinct overloads of the same method name remain distinct keys.
notes: regex and tree-sitter spellings are GROUND TRUTH captured from the current semidx extractor (semidx.runtime.languages.java/parse-file with default opts).

F1 RESOLVED (owner decision 2026-08-03): Variant C, precision-aware overload_identity. The heuristic tier commits arity only (signature_precision=arity_only, signature_key=null); the exact tier MAY add a typed signature. Stable unit identity anchors on the core key, not the typed hash. See reports/024, section 'F1 Resolution — Variant C'.

2026-08-28 (Stage 1): each distinct_facts_must_not_merge entry gained a structured expected_canonical_key. This restates the claim the prose already made so the fixture can be executed as a golden test instead of read by hand; no claim was changed.

2026-09-05 (Stage 4 preflight): the scip-java spelling was CORRECTED against real tool output and is now ground truth. The previously seeded 'representative' form claimed a scheme and a typed signature that scip-java does not emit; see scip_java_verified_contract below. The java-lsp spelling remains UNVERIFIED and was lowered to the conservative arity_only floor rather than left asserting a typed capability, because asserting an unverified exact-tier capability is the exact mistake this correction repairs. Stage 5 may raise it to typed only against real jdtls output.

2026-09-05: the Variant C claim 'the exact tier adds signature_precision=typed with a fully-qualified, type-only signature_key' is INVALIDATED FOR JAVA. It was never verified and is false for scip-java. Variant C's two-layer model (core key + optional refinement) is unchanged and still correct; only the premise that the Java exact tier can supply the refinement is withdrawn.

findings: Overloads are disambiguated by a SOURCE-ORDER ORDINAL, not by parameter types: the first declaration of a method name is `handle().`, the second is `handle(+1).`. The ordinal counts over the method NAME across all arities, not per arity.
The symbol carries NO parameter types and NO arity. Neither is recoverable from the moniker alone.

Arity and a human-readable signature are available only from SymbolInformation.signature_documentation.text, e.g. 'public String handle(String order, int retries)'. Its type names are SIMPLE and its parameter names are INCLUDED — the same shape the regex tier already produces, and the shape F1 rejected as Variant B.

Fully-qualified parameter types appear only as separate occurrences inside the method's declaration range (e.g. java/lang/String#). Reconstructing a typed signature from occurrence layout is inference, not a provider claim, and the plan forbids guessing a canonical key.
JDK and other external symbols carry a non-'.' package name (e.g. 'semanticdb maven jdk 17 java/lang/String#') and are correctly excluded as external.
A Java moniker carries the PACKAGE path (example/), not the source file path. The file path must come from Document.relative_path, unlike TypeScript where the moniker reconstructs it.
scip_java_verified_contract.consequence: The Java exact tier commits arity_only, exactly like the heuristic tier. The native symbol, the +N disambiguator, and the raw signature documentation are EVIDENCE ONLY and must never enter the canonical key.

provider_spellings.unverified_note: Stage 5 must capture this from real jdtls output. Held at the conservative arity_only floor until then: an unverified typed claim is what this fixture's 2026-09-05 correction exists to prevent. Raising it to typed is a fixture change that requires tool evidence.

expected_canonical_key.note: Variant C: unit identity anchors on core_key (owner, symbol, arity[, same-arity ordinal]). No Java provider currently supplies the typed refinement, so the merged precision is arity_only. The two-layer model is unchanged: if a future verified Java provider supplies a typed signature, it refines this fact WITHOUT changing its identity.

normalization_obligations: Variant C (owner decision 2026-08-03): overload_identity is precision-aware, not one fixed string.
Heuristic tier (regex/tree-sitter) emits signature_precision=arity_only, signature_key=null; it must NOT guess parameter types.

Java exact tier (scip-java) ALSO emits signature_precision=arity_only, signature_key=null (owner decision 2026-09-05). It must NOT reconstruct a typed signature from occurrence layout: that is inference, and a wrong key is worse than an honest arity-only one.
scip-java's native symbol, its +N source-order disambiguator, and its signature_documentation text are EVIDENCE ONLY and must never enter the canonical key.
Java arity is taken from SymbolInformation.signature_documentation.text; a method whose arity cannot be determined must be degraded, not guessed.

Stable unit identity anchors on the core key (owner, symbol, arity[, same-arity ordinal]); a typed signature, if a verified provider ever supplies one, is refining evidence and not part of the unit_id.
Same-arity overloads MUST NOT silently merge into one exact fact — see same_arity_overloads_must_not_silently_merge.

verified_defect.description: With every Java exact fact at arity_only, two genuinely distinct same-arity overloads share a core key and carry no typed signature to split on. fact-arbitration/arbitrate-facts takes its common-case branch (fewer than 2 distinct typed signatures) and merges them into ONE canonical fact at exact authority with ZERO diagnostics — a false exact identity.
verified_defect.reproduced_with: two arity-1 facts on example.OrderService#handle, both signature_precision=arity_only, native symbols handle(). and handle(+1).

required_behaviour: The Java adapter MUST detect a group of two or more definition facts sharing (language, path, owner, symbol, arity) where every fact is arity_only.
It MUST NOT emit a single exact canonical fact for that group.
It MUST emit a diagnostic identifying the ambiguous group.
It SHOULD withhold the exact contribution for that group and let the lower tiers supply the units, so no false exact identity is ever asserted.
Groups that are NOT ambiguous (a single definition per (owner, symbol, arity)) are unaffected and still merge with the heuristic tier on the core key.
same_arity_overloads_must_not_silently_m.note: The corpus OrderService has no same-arity overload pair (handle is arity 1 and arity 2), so this case is specified and tested synthetically. Adding a same-arity pair to the protected corpus would change the Stage 0 extraction baseline and is deliberately avoided.

distinct_facts_must_not_merge.reason: arity 2 vs arity 1 for the same method name; distinct overload.

scip_java_ground_truth.note: The +1 ordinal distinguishes it from handle(). in scip-java's own namespace only. Arity 2, parsed from the signature documentation, is what makes the canonical key distinct.

expected_canonical_overload_identity.note: Distinct core_key from arity 1; every tier separates it by arity alone, no ambiguity and no typed signature required.

distinct_facts_must_not_merge.reason: different method name and a generic parameter type; distinct symbol.

different owner/symbol; MUST NOT collide even though its regex signature hash (sig5e75e42b) is byte-identical to handle(String). A hash-only merge key would be unsafe; the canonical key must include owner+symbol+path, not only the signature hash.
